ko.title: [Logistics 101 #15] 재킷 한 벌, 열네 가지 교훈: 강의 전체를 한데 묶기

segments.src: > A supply chain is one long argument between speed, cost, and risk — and every company you shop at has picked a side.
segments.tr: > 공급망은 속도, 비용, 위험 사이의 긴 논쟁이다. 그리고 여러분이 쇼핑하는 모든 회사는 그중 한쪽 편을 들었다.
## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.
segments.tr: 이번이 강의의 마지막 시간이므로, 새로운 도구 대신 마지막 수업다운 일을 하겠습니다. 실제 기업 하나를 해부한 뒤, 무엇을 운송하든 계속 등장하는 몇 가지 아이디어를 짚어 보겠습니다.
**사례: 자라(Zara).**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: 자라는 스페인 북서부 아르테익소에 본사를 둔 인디텍스(Inditex)의 브랜드입니다.

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: 경쟁사들은 대부분 뻔한 방식을 택합니다. 시즌을 1년 앞서 디자인하고, 아시아의 가장 저렴한 공장에 대량으로 발주한 뒤, 태평양 너머로 배송하죠.

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: 이렇게 하면 *단위당* 비용이 가장 낮아지는데, 이것이 회의 자리에서 가장 쉽게 옹호되는 수치입니다.
자라는 다른 선택을 했습니다.

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: 유행에 민감한 품목, 즉 아무도 수요를 예측할 수 없는 상품은 스페인, 포르투갈, 모로코, 튀르키예에서 또는 그 인근에서 생산합니다.

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: 무지 티셔츠처럼 연중 꾸준히 팔리는 기본 아이템은 여전히 더 멀리 있는 저비용 공장에서 옵니다.

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: 매장은 대략 주 2회, 스타일별로 소량씩 물건을 받으며, 매장 관리자는 판매와 고객 반응을 본사에 끊임없이 피드백합니다.

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: 어떤 스타일이 실패하더라도 함께 사라지는 물량은 수백 벌뿐입니다.

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: 반대로 잘 팔리면, 시즌 단위가 아니라 몇 주 만에 더 많은 물량을 매장에 채울 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: 근거리 생산은 옷 한 벌당 비용이 더 듭니다.

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: 그 비용은 다른 곳에서 회수합니다. 자라는 재고 중 할인 판매하는 비율이 일반 패션 소매업체보다 낮은 것으로 널리 알려져 있으며, 정가에 팔리는 제품도 더 많습니다.

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: 가격 인하(마크다운)는 실제 비용입니다. 다만 그 비용이 소싱 담당자의 예산 항목에는 잡히지 않을 뿐이죠.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: 이 강의 전체의 교훈이 한 회사에 담겨 있습니다. **가장 저렴한 단위 원가가 곧 가장 저렴한 공급망은 아니다.** 쉬운 말로 정리하면 다음과 같습니다.
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: 1번 항목만 최적화하고 2번부터 5번까지를 무시하는 것이 이 분야에서 가장 흔하고 비싼 실수입니다.

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **강의에서 계속 되돌아온 다섯 가지 아이디어:**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **수요는 불확실하고, 불확실성에는 비용이 든다.** 그 비용은 필요 없던 재고로 치르거나, 팔지 못한 판매로 치르게 됩니다. 어느 쪽을 택할지는 고를 수 있지만, 둘 다 피할 수는 없습니다.

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **정보는 재고를 이긴다.** 채찍 효과(bullwhip effect), 즉 작은 수요 흔들림이 상류로 갈수록 거대한 진동으로 증폭되는 현상은 대부분 수학 문제가 아니라 소통 실패입니다.

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **속도는 예측의 대체재다.** 리드타임이 2주라면 거의 아무것도 예측할 필요가 없습니다. 9개월이라면 예측이 모든 일을 떠맡게 됩니다.

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **재고를 어디에 두느냐는 얼마나 두느냐만큼 중요하다.** 지연 설계(postponement), 풀링(pooling), 크로스도킹(cross-docking)은 모두 같은 직관입니다. 가능한 한 오래 범용적이고 중앙에 머무르고, 가능한 한 늦게 확정하라는 것이죠.

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **효율성과 회복탄력성은 반대 방향으로 당긴다.** 2011년 도호쿠 대지진 이후 도요타는 깊은 하위 공급 계층까지 지도를 그리고, 핵심 공급업체들에 반도체 완충 재고를 보유하도록 했습니다. 이는 말 그대로 린(lean) 방식과 어긋나는 행동이었습니다. 2021년 초 반도체 부족이 닥쳤을 때, 그 완충 재고 덕분에 도요타는 경쟁사들이 공장을 멈춰 세울 때도 생산을 계속할 수 있었습니다. 마법은 아니었습니다. 같은 해 후반, 동남아시아 공급업체들의 코로나19 봉쇄로 도요타도 결국 생산을 줄여야 했습니다. 회복탄력성은 시간을 사 줄 뿐, 면역을 주지는 않습니다.
## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: 8월 말 걸프 해안의 홈디포 매장을 한번 지켜보세요.

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: 홈디포는 애틀랜타 본사에서 허리케인 대응 지휘센터를 운영합니다.

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: 상륙 며칠 전부터 회사는 발전기, 합판, 식수, 방수포, 배터리를 예상 경로 근처의 집결지로 옮기기 시작합니다. 고객이 물건을 한 개도 사기 전이고, 정확히 어느 도시가 피해를 입을지 누구도 알기 전입니다.

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: 이 강의의 모든 아이디어가 그 결정 안에 들어 있습니다.

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **예측:** 태풍 경로 원뿔(storm cone)은 확률이지 약속이 아닙니다.

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **재고 배치:** 애틀랜타에 쌓인 재고는 목요일에 모빌에 있는 고객에게 쓸모가 없습니다. 잘못된 도시로 밀어낸 재고는 되돌려 실어 와야 하는 발전기 트럭 한 대분이 됩니다.

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **리드타임:** 고속도로가 막히면 보충 소요 시간이 하루에서 사실상 무한대로 늘어납니다. 그래서 결정은 일찍 내려야 하고, 가끔은 틀릴 수밖에 없습니다.

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **총비용:** 일주일 늦게 도착한 900달러짜리 발전기의 고객 가치는 거의 0에 가깝고, 폭풍 속에서 텅 빈 선반이 남기는 평판 손실은 어떤 청구서에도 담기지 않습니다.

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: 사전 배치를 하는 기업은 더 크고 정확히 측정할 수 없는 비용을 피하기 위해, 추가 운송비와 취급비를 알면서 감수하는 것입니다.
이것은 물류의 기교가 아닙니다.
이것이 바로 이 분야 전체입니다.
## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. 자라는 유행 상품을 가까이에서 만들기 위해 옷 한 벌당 더 많이 지불하고, 정가에 더 많이 팔아 그 비용을 회수합니다. 단위 원가는 실제 청구서의 한 항목일 뿐이라는 것을 보여 주는 사례입니다.

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. 반복되는 주제는 이렇습니다. 불확실성에는 언제나 비용이 들고, 정보는 재고를 대신할 수 있으며, 속도는 예측을 대신할 수 있고, 위치가 수량보다 중요하며, 회복탄력성은 공짜가 아니라 돈을 주고 사는 것입니다.

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. 모든 공급망 결정은 옷만 다를 뿐 결국 같은 결정입니다. 지금 얼마를 지불해야 나중에 덜 틀릴 수 있을까요?
## ✅ 자기 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** 한 소싱 담당자가 재킷 한 벌당 단위 원가를 2달러 낮추는 공장으로 바꿨습니다. 그런데 리드타임이 3주에서 4개월로 늘어납니다.

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: 어떤 비용이 절감액을 가장 상쇄할 가능성이 높을까요?
- (A) 통관 중개 수수료

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) 팔리지 않은 상품의 시즌 종료 할인

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) 구매 주문 소프트웨어 비용
- (D) 매장 인건비

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** O/X: 2011년 대지진 이후 구축된 도요타의 공급업체 반도체 완충 재고 덕분에, 회사는 2021년 반도체 부족 사태에 면역이 되었다.

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** 홈디포는 허리케인이 상륙하기 *전에* 발전기를 걸프 해안 쪽으로 보냅니다.
이것은 어떤 원리일까요?
- (A) 크로스도킹
- (B) 채찍 효과 증폭
- (C) 리드타임 제약 하의 재고 배치
- (D) 적시생산방식(JIT)
## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **총 착륙 비용(Total landed cost)**: 제품이 도착하기까지 드는 전체 비용입니다. 구매가에 운임, 관세, 재고 보관비, 가격 인하, 재고 부족 손실을 더한 금액입니다.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **근거리 생산(Nearshoring)**: 생산을 최종 시장 가까이로 옮기는 것입니다. 단위 원가는 높아지는 대신 리드타임이 짧고 더 민첩해집니다.

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **가격 인하(Markdown)**: 팔리지 않은 재고를 털어내기 위한 가격 인하입니다. 잘못된 예측의 직접적이고 측정 가능한 비용입니다.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **채찍 효과(Bullwhip effect)**: 주문이 소매업체에서 공급업체로 상류로 전달되면서 수요 변동이 증폭되는 현상입니다.

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **지연 설계(Postponement)**: 최종 구성을 수요가 확인될 때까지 정하지 않도록, 제품을 범용의 미확정 형태로 최대한 오래 유지하는 것입니다.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *정답: **1 — (B).** 긴 리드타임 때문에 무엇이 팔릴지 알기 전에 수량을 확정해야 합니다. 팔리지 않은 물량은 할인 판매되고, 그 가격 인하 비용은 보통 개당 2달러의 소싱 절감액을 훨씬 넘어섭니다.

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — X.** 완충 재고 덕분에 도요타는 2021년 초 경쟁사들이 라인을 멈춘 동안에도 생산을 이어 갈 수 있었지만, 그해 후반 동남아시아 공급업체들의 코로나19 봉쇄로 결국 생산 축소가 불가피했습니다.
회복탄력성은 시간을 사 줄 뿐, 면역을 주지는 않습니다.

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C).** 도로가 막히면 보충 리드타임은 사실상 무한대가 되므로, 재고는 사건이 일어나기 전에 올바른 곳에 있어야 합니다. 이는 생산이나 크로스도킹의 문제가 아니라 배치 결정입니다.*

zh.title: [物流学 101 #15] 一件夹克，十四堂课：把整门课串联起来

segments.src: > A supply chain is one long argument between speed, cost, and risk — and every company you shop at has picked a side.
segments.tr: > 供应链是速度、成本与风险之间一场漫长的辩论——而你购物的每一家公司，都已经站了队。
## 今日概念

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.
segments.tr: 这是本课程的最后一站。我们不引入新工具，而是做一堂结课课应有的事：拆解一家真实的公司，然后点出无论运送什么东西都会反复出现的几个核心观点。
**案例：Zara。**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: Zara 隶属于 Inditex 集团，总部位于西班牙西北部的阿尔泰肖（Arteixo）。

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: 其竞争对手大多采取显而易见的做法：提前一年设计每季产品，向亚洲成本最低的工厂下达大批量订单，再横跨太平洋运送。

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: 这种做法的单件成本最低，也是会议上最容易辩护的数字。
Zara 选择了另一种权衡。

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: 对于流行款式（那些无人能准确预测的商品），它在西班牙、葡萄牙、摩洛哥和土耳其本地或附近生产。

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: 而全年稳定热销的基础款，比如素色T恤，仍然来自更远但成本更低的工厂。

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: 门店大约每周收到两次补货，每个款式的数量都很少，店长则不断将销售情况和顾客反应反馈回总部。

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: 如果某个款式滞销，损失的只是几百件。

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: 如果卖得好，几周内就能把更多货品铺到店里，而不必等一整季。

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: 近岸生产让 Zara 每件服装的成本更高。

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: 它在其他环节把这笔钱赚了回来：据广泛报道，其打折清仓的库存比例低于一般时尚零售商，并且有更多商品以全价售出。

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: 降价清仓是真实的成本，只是它不出现在采购经理的预算表里。

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: 这门课的全部道理，凝练在这一家公司身上：**单位成本最低，并不等于供应链最便宜。** 用纯文字表示：
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: 只盯着第一行成本、却忽视第二到第五行的代价，是这个领域中最常见、也最昂贵的错误。

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **本课程反复强调的五个观点：**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **需求不确定，而不确定性是有代价的。** 你要么为用不上的库存买单，要么为卖不出去的销售机会买单。你可以选择付哪一种，但不能两样都不付。

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **信息胜过库存。** 牛鞭效应（需求的小幅波动在向上游传递时被放大成剧烈震荡）主要是沟通失灵的问题，而不是数学问题。

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **速度可以替代预测。** 如果你的交货周期是两周，几乎无需预测什么；如果是九个月，那么预测就得承担全部工作。

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **库存存放在哪里，与存多少同样重要。** 延迟策略（Postponement）、集中库存（Pooling）、越库作业（Cross-docking），都体现同一种思路：尽可能长时间保持通用和集中，并尽可能晚地做出承诺。

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **效率与韧性方向相反。** 2011 年东日本大地震之后，丰田梳理了其深层供应商层级，并让关键供应商为半导体保留缓冲库存，这是一种真正“不精益”的做法。2021 年初芯片短缺来临时，这些缓冲库存让丰田得以继续生产，而竞争对手的工厂却被迫停工。但这并非万能：2021 年晚些时候，东南亚供应商因新冠疫情停工，丰田同样不得不削减产量。韧性买来的是时间，而不是免疫力。
## 日常生活中的供应链

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: 请留意 8 月下旬墨西哥湾沿岸的一家家得宝（Home Depot）门店。

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: 家得宝在其位于亚特兰大的总部设有飓风指挥中心。

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: 在飓风登陆前几天，公司就开始把发电机、胶合板、饮用水、防水布和电池运往靠近预测路径的集散点。这时还没有任何顾客购买一件商品，也没有人确切知道哪座城市会受灾。

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: 本课程的每一个观点都体现在这个决策中。

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **预测：** 飓风路径锥只是一种概率，而不是承诺。

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **库存布局：** 存放在亚特兰大的货品对周四身处莫比尔市的顾客毫无用处；而如果货品被送到错误的都会区，你就得再花钱把一卡车发电机运回来。

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **交货周期：** 一旦高速公路封闭，补货时间就从一天变成了无限长，因此决策必须提前做出，并且注定有时会出错。

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **总成本：** 一台 900 美元的发电机如果晚到一周，对顾客的价值几乎为零；而暴风雨期间货架空空所带来的声誉损失，则无法体现在任何一张发票上。

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: 提前布局的公司，是在有意识地接受额外的运费和处理成本，以避免一项更大、却难以精确衡量的成本。
这并不是什么物流技巧。
这正是整个学科的核心。
## 三句话总结

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. Zara 为了在近岸生产流行款式，每件服装多付出了成本，但又通过全价销售更多商品把它赚了回来。这证明单位成本只是真实账单中的一项。

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. 反复出现的主题是：不确定性总会带来代价；信息可以替代库存；速度可以替代预测；位置比数量更重要；而韧性需要花钱去买，并非免费。

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. 每一个供应链决策，本质上都是同一个决策换了件衣服：你愿意现在多付出多少，来换取将来少犯一些错误？
## ✅ 自我测验

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** 一位采购经理改用一家工厂，每件夹克的单位成本降低 2 美元，但交货周期从 3 周延长到 4 个月。

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: 哪一项成本**最有可能**抵消这笔节省？
- (A) 清关经纪费

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) 当季未售出款式的季末降价清仓

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) 采购订单软件的成本
- (D) 门店人工成本

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** 判断对错（O/X）：丰田在 2011 年地震后建立的供应商芯片缓冲库存，使公司免受 2021 年半导体短缺的影响。

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** 家得宝在飓风**登陆之前**就把发电机运往墨西哥湾沿岸。
这体现的是什么原则？
- (A) 越库作业（Cross-docking）
- (B) 牛鞭效应的放大
- (C) 交货周期约束下的库存布局
- (D) 准时制生产（JIT）
## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **总到岸成本（Total landed cost）**：产品交付到手的完整成本，包括采购价，以及运费、关税、持有成本、降价清仓损失和缺货损失。

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **近岸外包（Nearshoring）**：将生产转移到更靠近终端市场的地方，以更高的单位成本换取更短、更灵活的交货周期。

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **降价清仓（Markdown）**：为清理未售出的库存而进行的降价，是错误预测直接、可衡量的成本。

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **牛鞭效应（Bullwhip effect）**：订单从零售商向供应商逐级向上游传递时，需求波动被不断放大的现象。

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **延迟策略（Postponement）**：让产品尽可能长时间保持通用、尚未定型的状态，待需求明确后再确定最终配置。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *答案：**1 — (B)。** 较长的交货周期迫使你在知道什么会卖得好之前就确定数量；卖不掉的单位会被降价，而降价损失通常远大于每件 2 美元的采购节省。

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — X。** 缓冲库存帮助丰田在 2021 年初继续生产，而竞争对手的生产线却已停工；但同年晚些时候，东南亚供应商因疫情停工，丰田仍不得不削减产量。
韧性买来的是时间，而不是免疫力。

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C)。** 道路封闭后，补货的交货周期实际上变成无限长，因此库存必须在事件发生之前就放在正确的位置。这是一个布局决策，而不是生产或越库决策。*

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **पाँच विचार जिन पर कोर्स बार-बार लौटता रहा:**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **माँग अनिश्चित है, और अनिश्चितता की कीमत चुकानी पड़ती है।** आप इसे या तो ऐसी इन्वेंट्री के रूप में चुकाते हैं जिसकी आपको ज़रूरत नहीं थी, या ऐसी बिक्री के रूप में जो आप नहीं कर पाए। चुनाव आपका है — आपके पास "कोई नुकसान नहीं" का विकल्प नहीं है।

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **जानकारी, इन्वेंट्री से बेहतर है।** Bullwhip effect — माँग में छोटे उतार-चढ़ाव का ऊपर की ओर जाकर भारी झटकों में बदल जाना — मुख्य रूप से एक संचार की विफलता है, गणित की समस्या नहीं।

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **गति, पूर्वानुमान का विकल्प है।** अगर आपका lead time दो हफ़्ते है, तो आपको शायद ही कुछ अनुमान लगाना पड़ता है। अगर यह नौ महीने है, तो आपका पूर्वानुमान ही सारा काम कर रहा होता है।

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **इन्वेंट्री कहाँ रखी है, यह उतना ही मायने रखता है जितना कि कितनी रखी है।** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — इन सबके पीछे एक ही सोच है: जितना लंबा हो सके सामान्य और केंद्रीय बने रहें, और जितनी देर से हो सके प्रतिबद्ध हों।

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **कुशलता और लचीलापन विपरीत दिशाओं में खींचते हैं।** 2011 के Tōhoku भूकंप के बाद, Toyota ने अपने गहरे सप्लायर स्तरों का नक्शा बनाया और मुख्य सप्लायरों से सेमीकंडक्टर का बफ़र स्टॉक रखवाया — यह सचमुच lean सोच के विरुद्ध व्यवहार था। 2021 की शुरुआत में जब चिप की कमी आई, तो इस बफ़र की वजह से Toyota उत्पादन जारी रख सका, जबकि प्रतिस्पर्धी प्लांट बंद रखने को मजबूर हुए। यह कोई जादू नहीं था: 2021 में बाद में, दक्षिण-पूर्व एशियाई सप्लायरों में COVID बंदी के कारण Toyota को भी उत्पादन घटाना पड़ा। लचीलापन आपको समय देता है, प्रतिरक्षा नहीं।
## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: अगस्त के अंत में Gulf Coast पर किसी Home Depot को देखिए।

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: Home Depot अपने Atlanta मुख्यालय से एक hurricane command center चलाता है।

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: तूफ़ान के टकराने से कुछ दिन पहले, कंपनी जनरेटर, प्लाईवुड, पानी, तिरपाल और बैटरियाँ पूर्वानुमानित रास्ते के पास staging points की ओर भेजना शुरू कर देती है — किसी ग्राहक द्वारा एक भी सामान खरीदने से पहले, और यह जाने बिना कि ठीक कौन-सा शहर प्रभावित होगा।

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: इस कोर्स का हर विचार उस निर्णय में मौजूद है।

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **पूर्वानुमान:** तूफ़ान का "cone" एक संभावना है, कोई वादा नहीं।

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **इन्वेंट्री की स्थिति:** Atlanta में रखा स्टॉक गुरुवार को Mobile के ग्राहक के किसी काम का नहीं; और गलत महानगर में भेजा गया स्टॉक जनरेटरों से भरा एक ट्रक है, जिसे अब वापस ढोना पड़ेगा।

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **Lead time:** एक बार हाईवे बंद हो जाएँ, तो आपका replenishment समय एक दिन से अनंत हो जाता है, इसलिए निर्णय पहले लेना होगा और कभी-कभी गलत भी होगा।

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **कुल लागत:** $900 का जनरेटर, जो एक हफ़्ता देर से पहुँचे, उसका ग्राहक-मूल्य लगभग शून्य है, और तूफ़ान के दौरान खाली शेल्फ़ों से होने वाला प्रतिष्ठा का नुकसान किसी इनवॉइस में नहीं समाता।

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: जो कंपनी पहले से पहुँचाती है, वह जानबूझकर अतिरिक्त माल ढुलाई और हैंडलिंग की लागत स्वीकार करती है, ताकि एक कहीं बड़ी लागत से बच सके जिसे वह सटीक रूप से माप नहीं सकती।
यह कोई logistics की चाल नहीं है।
यही पूरा अनुशासन है।
## तीन पंक्तियों में सार

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. Zara हर गारमेंट पर ज़्यादा खर्च करके रुझान वाली वस्तुएँ घर के करीब बनाता है, और उसे पूरी कीमत पर ज़्यादा बेचकर वापस कमाता है — यह इस बात का प्रमाण है कि असली बिल में प्रति-इकाई लागत बस एक पंक्ति है।

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. बार-बार आने वाले विषय: अनिश्चितता हमेशा कुछ कीमत लेती है, जानकारी इन्वेंट्री का विकल्प बनती है, गति पूर्वानुमान का विकल्प बनती है, स्थिति मात्रा से बेहतर है, और लचीलापन खरीदा जाता है, मुफ़्त नहीं मिलता।

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. हर आपूर्ति श्रृंखला का निर्णय, अलग कपड़ों में वही निर्णय है — आप आज कितना भुगतान करने को तैयार हैं, ताकि बाद में कम गलत साबित हों?
## ✅ स्व-प्रश्नोत्तरी

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** एक सोर्सिंग मैनेजर एक ऐसी फ़ैक्ट्री पर स्विच करता है जो हर जैकेट की प्रति-इकाई लागत $2 घटाती है, लेकिन lead time 3 हफ़्ते से बढ़कर 4 महीने हो जाता है।

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: कौन-सी लागत सबसे अधिक संभावना से इस बचत को मिटा देगी?
- (A) कस्टम्स ब्रोकरेज शुल्क

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) उन स्टाइलों पर सीज़न-अंत की markdown, जो नहीं बिके

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) Purchase order सॉफ़्टवेयर की लागत
- (D) स्टोर का श्रम

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** O/X — 2011 के भूकंप के बाद बनाए गए Toyota के सप्लायर चिप बफ़र ने कंपनी को 2021 की सेमीकंडक्टर कमी से पूरी तरह अप्रभावित बना दिया।

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** Home Depot तूफ़ान के टकराने *से पहले* जनरेटर Gulf Coast की ओर भेजता है।
यह कौन-सा सिद्धांत है?
- (A) Cross-docking
- (B) Bullwhip amplification
- (C) Lead-time सीमाओं के तहत इन्वेंट्री स्थिति निर्धारण
- (D) Just-in-time उत्पादन
## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **Total landed cost** — किसी उत्पाद की पूरी डिलीवर्ड लागत: खरीद मूल्य के साथ माल ढुलाई, शुल्क, भंडारण लागत, markdown और stockout से होने वाला नुकसान।

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring** — उत्पादन को अंतिम बाज़ार के करीब ले जाना, जिसमें प्रति इकाई ऊँची लागत के बदले छोटे और अधिक प्रतिक्रियाशील lead time मिलते हैं।

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **Markdown** — न बिकी इन्वेंट्री निपटाने के लिए ली गई कीमत में कटौती; खराब पूर्वानुमान की सीधी, मापने योग्य लागत।

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **Bullwhip effect** — रिटेलर से सप्लायर तक ऑर्डर ऊपर की ओर जाते समय माँग में उतार-चढ़ाव का बढ़ जाना।

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **Postponement** — किसी उत्पाद को यथासंभव लंबे समय तक सामान्य, अप्रतिबद्ध रूप में रखना, ताकि माँग जानने के बाद अंतिम विन्यास तय किया जा सके।

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **1 — (B).** लंबे lead time का मतलब है कि आपको यह जाने बिना मात्रा तय करनी पड़ती है कि क्या बिकेगा; न बिके माल पर छूट दी जाती है, और यह markdown आमतौर पर $2 प्रति इकाई की सोर्सिंग बचत से कहीं ज़्यादा होती है।

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — X.** बफ़र ने 2021 की शुरुआत में Toyota को प्रतिस्पर्धियों के लाइनें बंद रखने के दौरान उत्पादन जारी रखने में मदद की, लेकिन उसी साल बाद में दक्षिण-पूर्व एशियाई सप्लायरों में COVID बंदी से उत्पादन में कटौती फिर भी करनी पड़ी।
लचीलापन समय खरीदता है, प्रतिरक्षा नहीं।

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C).** सड़कें बंद होने के बाद replenishment lead time व्यावहारिक रूप से अनंत हो जाता है, इसलिए घटना से पहले इन्वेंट्री सही जगह पर होनी चाहिए — यह स्थिति-निर्धारण का निर्णय है, उत्पादन या docking का नहीं.*

es.title: [Logística 101 #15] Una chaqueta, catorce lecciones: el curso completo en una sola idea

segments.src: > A supply chain is one long argument between speed, cost, and risk — and every company you shop at has picked a side.
segments.tr: > Una cadena de suministro es un largo debate entre velocidad, costo y riesgo, y cada empresa en la que compras ha elegido un bando.
## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.
segments.tr: Esta es la última parada del curso, así que en lugar de una herramienta nueva haremos lo que debería hacer una clase final: desmontar una empresa real y luego nombrar el puñado de ideas que siguen apareciendo sin importar qué se esté transportando.
**El caso: Zara.**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: Zara pertenece a Inditex, con sede en Arteixo, en el noroeste de España.

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: Sus competidores, en su mayoría, hacen lo obvio: diseñan una temporada con un año de antelación, realizan enormes pedidos a las fábricas de menor costo de Asia y los envían cruzando el Pacífico.

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: Eso produce el costo más bajo *por unidad*, que es la cifra más fácil de defender en una reunión.
Zara hizo un intercambio distinto.

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: Los artículos sensibles a las tendencias, los que nadie puede pronosticar, se fabrican en España, Portugal, Marruecos o Turquía, o cerca de ellos.

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: Los básicos que se venden de forma constante durante todo el año, como las camisetas lisas, siguen procediendo de fábricas de menor costo y más lejanas.

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: Las tiendas reciben envíos aproximadamente dos veces por semana, en pequeñas cantidades por modelo, y los gerentes de tienda devuelven constantemente información sobre las ventas y las reacciones de los clientes.

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: Si un modelo fracasa, solo se pierden unos cientos de unidades con él.

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: Si se vende, pueden llegar más unidades a las tiendas en semanas en lugar de temporadas.

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: La producción cercana le cuesta más a Zara por prenda.

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: Recupera ese dinero en otra parte: según se informa ampliamente, rebaja una proporción menor de su inventario que los minoristas de moda típicos, y vende más producto a precio completo.

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: Una rebaja es un costo real; simplemente no aparece en la partida presupuestaria del gerente de abastecimiento.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: Esa es toda la lección del curso en una sola empresa: **el costo unitario más bajo no es la cadena de suministro más barata.** En texto plano:
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: Optimizar la línea uno mientras se ignoran las líneas dos a cinco es el error costoso más común en este campo.

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **Cinco ideas a las que el curso volvió una y otra vez:**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **La demanda es incierta, y la incertidumbre cuesta dinero.** La pagas, ya sea en forma de inventario que no necesitabas o de ventas que no pudiste realizar. Tú eliges cuál; no puedes elegir ninguna de las dos.

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **La información vale más que el inventario.** El efecto látigo (pequeñas oscilaciones de la demanda que se amplifican hasta convertirse en fuertes vaivenes aguas arriba) es sobre todo un fallo de comunicación, no un problema matemático.

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **La velocidad sustituye a la previsión.** Si tu plazo de entrega es de dos semanas, casi no necesitas predecir nada. Si es de nueve meses, tu pronóstico hace todo el trabajo.

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **Dónde mantienes el inventario importa tanto como cuánto.** El aplazamiento (postponement), la agrupación (pooling) y el cross-docking responden todos al mismo instinto: mantente genérico y centralizado el mayor tiempo posible, y compromete las decisiones lo más tarde posible.

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **La eficiencia y la resiliencia tiran en direcciones opuestas.** Después del terremoto de Tōhoku de 2011, Toyota mapeó sus niveles profundos de proveedores y pidió a los proveedores clave que mantuvieran existencias de seguridad de semiconductores, un comportamiento genuinamente no esbelto. Cuando la escasez de chips golpeó a comienzos de 2021, ese colchón permitió a Toyota seguir produciendo mientras sus rivales paralizaban sus plantas. No fue magia: más adelante, en 2021, los cierres por COVID en proveedores del sudeste asiático obligaron también a Toyota a recortar su producción. La resiliencia te compra tiempo, no inmunidad.
## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: Observa un Home Depot en la costa del Golfo a finales de agosto.

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: Home Depot dirige un centro de mando para huracanes desde su sede central en Atlanta.

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: Días antes de que toque tierra, la empresa empieza a trasladar generadores, madera contrachapada, agua, lonas y baterías a puntos de preparación cercanos a la trayectoria pronosticada, antes de que cualquier cliente haya comprado un solo artículo y antes de que nadie sepa con exactitud qué ciudad será golpeada.

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: Cada idea de este curso está en esa decisión.

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **Previsión:** el cono de la tormenta es una probabilidad, no una promesa.

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **Posicionamiento del inventario:** el stock que está en Atlanta no le sirve a un cliente en Mobile el jueves; el stock enviado a la área metropolitana equivocada es un camión de generadores que ahora tienes que devolver.

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **Plazo de entrega:** una vez cerradas las carreteras, tu tiempo de reabastecimiento pasa de un día a infinito, así que la decisión tiene que tomarse pronto y a veces equivocarse.

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **Costo total:** un generador de 900 dólares que llega una semana tarde tiene un valor para el cliente de prácticamente cero, y el costo reputacional de las estanterías vacías durante una tormenta no cabe en ninguna factura.

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: La empresa que se adelanta acepta conscientemente gastos extra de flete y manipulación para evitar un costo mucho mayor que no puede medir con precisión.
Eso no es un truco logístico.
Esa es toda la disciplina.
## Resumen en tres líneas

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.

## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **Costo total puesto en destino (total landed cost)**: el costo completo entregado de un producto, es decir, el precio de compra más el flete, los aranceles, el costo de mantenimiento, las rebajas y las pérdidas por falta de stock.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **Producción cercana (nearshoring)**: trasladar la producción más cerca del mercado final, cambiando un costo unitario más alto por plazos de entrega más cortos y una respuesta más ágil.

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **Rebaja (markdown)**: reducción de precio aplicada para liquidar inventario que no se vendió; es un costo directo y medible de una mala previsión.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **Efecto látigo (bullwhip effect)**: la amplificación de las oscilaciones de la demanda a medida que los pedidos viajan aguas arriba, del minorista al proveedor.

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **Aplazamiento (postponement)**: mantener un producto en una forma genérica y sin comprometer el mayor tiempo posible, para que la configuración final pueda decidirse una vez conocida la demanda.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.

segments.src: > A supply chain is one long argument between speed, cost, and risk — and every company you shop at has picked a side.
segments.tr: > سلسلة الإمداد هي حجّة طويلة واحدة بين السرعة والتكلفة والمخاطرة، وكل شركة تتسوق منها اختارت جانبًا.
## محور اليوم

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.
segments.tr: هذه هي المحطة الأخيرة في الدورة، لذا بدلًا من أداة جديدة سنفعل ما ينبغي أن يفعله الدرس الختامي: نفكك شركة حقيقية واحدة، ثم نسمي حفنة من الأفكار التي تتكرر مهما كان ما تنقله.
**الحالة: Zara.**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: تنتمي Zara إلى Inditex، ومقرها في Arteixo شمال غرب إسبانيا.

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: ينفذ منافسوها في الغالب الأمر البديهي: يصممون موسمًا قبل عام، ويقدّمون طلبات ضخمة لأرخص المصانع في آسيا، ويشحنونها عبر المحيط الهادئ.

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: وهذا ينتج أدنى تكلفة *للوحدة*، وهو الرقم الأسهل دفاعًا عنه في الاجتماعات.
أما Zara فاتخذت مقايضة مختلفة.

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: تُصنع القطع الحساسة للموضة، أي تلك التي لا يستطيع أحد التنبؤ بالطلب عليها، في إسبانيا أو البرتغال أو المغرب أو تركيا أو بالقرب منها.

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: أما الأساسيات التي تُباع بثبات طوال العام، مثل التيشيرتات البسيطة، فما زالت تأتي من مصانع أقل تكلفة وأبعد.

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: تصل الشحنات إلى المتاجر نحو مرتين أسبوعيًا، بكميات صغيرة لكل طراز، ويرسل مديرو المتاجر باستمرار بيانات المبيعات وردود فعل الزبائن.

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: إذا فشل طراز، لا تخسر الشركة سوى بضع مئات من القطع.

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: وإذا نجح، يمكن أن تصل كميات إضافية إلى المتاجر خلال أسابيع بدلًا من مواسم.

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: يكلّف التصنيع القريب Zara تكلفة أعلى للقطعة.

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: لكنها تستعيد هذا المال من مكان آخر: يُذكر على نطاق واسع أنها تُخفّض أسعارًا على جزء أصغر من مخزونها مقارنة بتجار الأزياء المعتادين، وتبيع كمية أكبر من المنتجات بالسعر الكامل.

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: التخفيض السعري تكلفة حقيقية، لكنها لا تظهر في بند ميزانية مدير المشتريات.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: هذا هو درس الدورة كله في شركة واحدة: **أدنى تكلفة للوحدة ليست أرخص سلسلة إمداد.** وبنص عادي:
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: تحسين السطر الأول مع تجاهل السطور من الثاني إلى الخامس هو أكثر الأخطاء المكلفة شيوعًا في هذا المجال.

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **خمس أفكار عادت إليها الدورة مرارًا:**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **الطلب غير مؤكد، وعدم اليقين له ثمن.** تدفعه إما كمخزون لم تكن بحاجته، أو كمبيعات لم تستطع تحقيقها. أنت تختار أيهما، ولا يُتاح لك أن تختار ألا تدفع شيئًا.

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **المعلومات تتفوق على المخزون.** تأثير السوط (Bullwhip)، أي تذبذبات صغيرة في الطلب تتضخم إلى تأرجحات عنيفة في المراحل الأعلى من السلسلة، هو في الأغلب فشل في التواصل لا مسألة رياضية.

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **السرعة بديل عن التنبؤ.** إذا كان زمن التوريد أسبوعين، فأنت بالكاد تحتاج إلى التنبؤ بشيء. وإذا كان تسعة أشهر، فإن توقعك هو الذي يقوم بكل العمل.

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **مكان تخزين المخزون لا يقل أهمية عن كميته.** التأجيل (Postponement) والتجميع (Pooling) والعبور المباشر (Cross-docking): كلها تنبع من غريزة واحدة، وهي أن تبقى عامًا ومركزيًا قدر الإمكان، وأن تلتزم متأخرًا قدر الإمكان.

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **الكفاءة والمرونة تسيران في اتجاهين متعاكسين.** بعد زلزال توهوكو عام 2011، رسمت Toyota خريطة لطبقات مورديها العميقة، وطلبت من الموردين الرئيسيين الاحتفاظ بمخزون احتياطي من أشباه الموصلات، وهو سلوك غير رشيق فعلًا. وعندما ضرب نقص الرقائق أوائل عام 2021، مكّنها ذلك المخزون الاحتياطي من مواصلة الإنتاج بينما توقفت مصانع منافسيها. لم يكن الأمر سحريًا: ففي وقت لاحق من عام 2021، أجبرت عمليات إغلاق بسبب كوفيد لدى موردين في جنوب شرق آسيا Toyota على خفض إنتاجها أيضًا. المرونة تشتري لك الوقت، لا الحصانة.

fr.title: [Logistique 101 #15] Une veste, quatorze leçons : tout réunir en fin de cours

segments.src: > A supply chain is one long argument between speed, cost, and risk — and every company you shop at has picked a side.
segments.tr: > Une chaîne d'approvisionnement est un long argument entre vitesse, coût et risque, et chaque entreprise dont vous êtes client a choisi son camp.
## Concept du jour

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.
segments.tr: C'est la dernière étape du cours. Plutôt que de présenter un nouvel outil, nous allons faire ce que doit faire un dernier cours : disséquer une entreprise réelle, puis nommer une poignée d'idées qui reviennent systématiquement, quelle que soit la marchandise transportée.
**L'étude de cas : Zara.**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: Zara appartient à Inditex, dont le siège se trouve à Arteixo, dans le nord-ouest de l'Espagne.

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: Ses concurrents font pour la plupart la chose évidente : concevoir une saison un an à l'avance, passer d'énormes commandes auprès des usines asiatiques les moins chères et les expédier à travers le Pacifique.

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: Cela produit le coût le plus bas *par unité*, le chiffre le plus facile à défendre en réunion.
Zara a fait un arbitrage différent.

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: Les articles sensibles aux tendances, ceux que personne ne peut prévoir, sont fabriqués en Espagne, au Portugal, au Maroc ou en Turquie, ou à proximité.

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: Les basiques qui se vendent régulièrement toute l'année, comme les t-shirts unis, proviennent toujours d'usines à bas coût plus éloignées.

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: Les magasins reçoivent des livraisons environ deux fois par semaine, en petites quantités par modèle, et les responsables de magasin font remonter en permanence les ventes et les réactions des clients.

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: Si un modèle ne prend pas, seules quelques centaines d'unités sont perdues avec lui.

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: S'il se vend, davantage d'unités peuvent être en magasin en quelques semaines plutôt qu'en plusieurs saisons.

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: La production de proximité coûte plus cher par vêtement.

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: Zara compense ailleurs : elle solde, selon les informations largement relayées, une part de son stock moins importante que les détaillants de mode habituels, et vend davantage de produits à plein prix.

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: Une démarque est un coût réel, simplement il n'apparaît pas dans la ligne budgétaire du responsable achats.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: C'est toute la leçon du cours résumée en une entreprise : **le coût unitaire le plus bas n'est pas la chaîne d'approvisionnement la moins chère.** En clair :
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: Optimiser la ligne un en ignorant les lignes deux à cinq est l'erreur coûteuse la plus courante dans ce domaine.

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **Cinq idées auxquelles le cours n'a cessé de revenir :**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **La demande est incertaine, et l'incertitude coûte de l'argent.** On la paie soit en stock inutile, soit en ventes perdues. Vous choisissez lequel : vous ne pouvez pas choisir aucun des deux.

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **L'information vaut mieux que le stock.** L'effet coup de fouet (bullwhip) — de petites oscillations de la demande qui s'amplifient en fortes variations en amont — est surtout un problème de communication, pas de calcul.

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **La rapidité remplace la prévision.** Si votre délai est de deux semaines, vous n'avez presque rien à prédire. S'il est de neuf mois, c'est votre prévision qui fait tout le travail.

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **L'endroit où l'on stocke compte autant que la quantité.** Report de différenciation (postponement), mutualisation (pooling), cross-docking : tout cela relève du même réflexe, rester générique et centralisé le plus longtemps possible, et s'engager le plus tard possible.

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **Efficacité et résilience tirent dans des directions opposées.** Après le séisme de Tōhoku en 2011, Toyota a cartographié les niveaux profonds de ses fournisseurs et a fait constituer à ses fournisseurs clés des stocks tampons de semi-conducteurs, un comportement véritablement non lean. Quand la pénurie de puces a frappé au début de 2021, ce tampon a permis à Toyota de continuer à produire pendant que ses rivaux arrêtaient leurs usines. Ce n'était pas magique : plus tard en 2021, les fermetures liées à la COVID chez des fournisseurs d'Asie du Sud-Est ont obligé Toyota à réduire aussi sa production. La résilience achète du temps, pas l'immunité.
## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: Observez un Home Depot sur la côte du Golfe fin août.

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: Home Depot gère un centre de commandement pour les ouragans depuis son siège d'Atlanta.

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: Quelques jours avant l'arrivée de la tempête, l'entreprise commence à acheminer groupes électrogènes, contreplaqué, eau, bâches et piles vers des points de stockage proches de la trajectoire prévue, avant qu'un seul client n'ait acheté quoi que ce soit, et avant que quiconque sache exactement quelle ville sera touchée.

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: Toutes les idées de ce cours figurent dans cette décision.

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **Prévision :** le cône de la tempête est une probabilité, pas une promesse.

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **Positionnement des stocks :** un stock qui reste à Atlanta ne sert à rien à un client de Mobile jeudi ; un stock envoyé dans la mauvaise zone métropolitaine, c'est un camion de groupes électrogènes qu'il faudra ensuite ramener.

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **Délai :** une fois les autoroutes fermées, votre délai de réapprovisionnement passe d'un jour à l'infini, donc la décision doit être prise tôt et sera parfois fausse.

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **Coût total :** un groupe électrogène à 900 $ qui arrive une semaine en retard a une valeur client proche de zéro, et le coût pour la réputation de rayons vides pendant une tempête ne figure sur aucune facture.

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: L'entreprise qui pré-positionne accepte sciemment des frais de transport et de manutention supplémentaires pour éviter un coût bien plus important qu'elle ne peut pas mesurer précisément.
Ce n'est pas une astuce logistique.
C'est toute la discipline.
## Résumé en trois points

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. Zara paie plus cher par vêtement pour fabriquer les articles tendance près de chez elle, et le rattrape en vendant davantage à plein prix, preuve que le coût unitaire n'est qu'une ligne de la facture réelle.

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. Les thèmes récurrents : l'incertitude coûte toujours quelque chose, l'information se substitue au stock, la rapidité se substitue à la prévision, le positionnement vaut mieux que la quantité, et la résilience s'achète, elle n'est pas gratuite.

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. Chaque décision de chaîne d'approvisionnement est la même décision sous d'autres habits : combien êtes-vous prêt à payer maintenant pour vous tromper moins plus tard ?
## ✅ Auto-évaluation

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** Un responsable achats passe à une usine qui réduit le coût unitaire de 2 $ par veste, mais le délai passe de 3 semaines à 4 mois.

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: Quel coût est le PLUS susceptible d'effacer cette économie ?
- (A) Frais de courtage en douane

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) Démarques de fin de saison sur les modèles qui ne se sont pas vendus

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) Le coût du logiciel de bons de commande
- (D) Le coût de la main-d'œuvre en magasin

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** V/F : les tampons de puces de Toyota chez ses fournisseurs, constitués après le séisme de 2011, ont rendu l'entreprise immunisée contre la pénurie de semi-conducteurs de 2021.

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** Home Depot achemine des groupes électrogènes vers la côte du Golfe *avant* que l'ouragan ne touche terre.
Quel principe est-ce ?
- (A) Cross-docking
- (B) Amplification de l'effet coup de fouet
- (C) Positionnement des stocks sous contrainte de délai
- (D) Production en flux tendu (juste-à-temps)
## 📚 Termes du jour

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **Coût total rendu (total landed cost)** — le coût complet de livraison d'un produit : prix d'achat plus fret, droits de douane, coût de possession du stock, démarques et pertes dues aux ruptures.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring** — rapprocher la production du marché final, en échangeant un coût unitaire plus élevé contre des délais plus courts et une réactivité accrue.

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **Démarque (markdown)** — une baisse de prix appliquée pour écouler un stock invendu ; coût direct et mesurable d'une mauvaise prévision.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **Effet coup de fouet (bullwhip effect)** — l'amplification des variations de la demande à mesure que les commandes remontent du détaillant vers le fournisseur.

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **Report de différenciation (postponement)** — maintenir un produit sous une forme générique et non engagée le plus longtemps possible, afin de pouvoir décider de la configuration finale une fois la demande connue.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *Réponses : **1 — (B).** Les longs délais obligent à fixer les quantités avant de savoir ce qui se vendra ; les unités invendues sont soldées, et les démarques dépassent généralement une économie d'achat de 2 $ par unité.

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — F.** Les tampons ont aidé Toyota à continuer de produire au début de 2021 pendant que ses concurrents arrêtaient leurs lignes, mais plus tard dans l'année, les fermetures liées à la COVID chez des fournisseurs d'Asie du Sud-Est ont quand même forcé des réductions de production.
La résilience achète du temps, pas l'immunité.

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C).** Une fois les routes fermées, le délai de réapprovisionnement devient effectivement infini, donc les stocks doivent être au bon endroit avant l'événement : une décision de positionnement, ni de production ni de cross-docking.*
