segments.tr: 5. **Eficiência e resiliência puxam em direções opostas.** Depois do terremoto de Tōhoku, em 2011, a Toyota mapeou as camadas profundas de fornecedores e fez com que fornecedores-chave mantivessem estoque de segurança de semicondutores, um comportamento genuinamente não enxuto. Quando a escassez de chips atingiu o setor, no início de 2021, esse estoque permitiu à Toyota continuar produzindo enquanto concorrentes paralisavam fábricas. Não foi mágica: ainda em 2021, fechamentos por causa da COVID em fornecedores do Sudeste Asiático obrigaram a Toyota a cortar produção também. A resiliência compra tempo, não imunidade.
## No Dia a Dia

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: Observe uma Home Depot na Costa do Golfo no fim de agosto.

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: A Home Depot opera um centro de comando para furacões a partir da sede em Atlanta.

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: Dias antes da chegada da tempestade, a empresa começa a deslocar geradores, compensado, água, lonas e baterias para pontos de apoio próximos à trajetória prevista, antes que qualquer cliente tenha comprado um único item e antes que alguém saiba exatamente qual cidade será atingida.

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: Todas as ideias deste curso estão nessa decisão.

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **Previsão:** o cone da tempestade é uma probabilidade, não uma promessa.

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **Posicionamento de estoque:** o estoque parado em Atlanta não serve para um cliente em Mobile na quinta-feira; estoque enviado à região metropolitana errada vira uma carreta de geradores que você agora precisa trazer de volta.

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **Lead time:** quando as rodovias fecham, o tempo de reposição passa de um dia para infinito, então a decisão precisa ser tomada cedo e às vezes estará errada.

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **Custo total:** um gerador de US$ 900 que chega uma semana atrasada tem valor para o cliente próximo de zero, e o custo de reputação de prateleiras vazias durante uma tempestade não cabe em nenhuma nota fiscal.

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: A empresa que faz a pré-posição aceita, de forma consciente, custos extras de frete e manuseio para evitar um custo muito maior que não consegue medir com precisão.
Isso não é um truque de logística.
É a disciplina inteira.
## Resumo em Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. A Zara paga mais por peça para produzir itens de tendência perto de casa e recupera esse valor vendendo mais por preço cheio. Isso prova que o custo unitário é apenas uma linha da conta real.

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. Os temas recorrentes são: a incerteza sempre custa algo, a informação substitui estoque, a velocidade substitui previsão, a posição vale mais que a quantidade, e a resiliência se compra, não é grátis.

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. Toda decisão de cadeia de suprimentos é a mesma decisão com roupas diferentes: quanto você está disposto a pagar agora para errar menos depois?
## ✅ Autoavaliação

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** Um gerente de compras troca para uma fábrica que reduz o custo unitário em US$ 2 por jaqueta, mas o lead time passa de 3 semanas para 4 meses.

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: Qual custo tem MAIOR probabilidade de anular a economia?
- (A) Taxas de despachante aduaneiro

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) Liquidações de fim de temporada em modelos que não venderam

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) O custo do software de pedidos de compra
- (D) Mão de obra da loja

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** V/F: os estoques de segurança de chips dos fornecedores da Toyota, criados após o terremoto de 2011, tornaram a empresa imune à escassez de semicondutores de 2021.

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** A Home Depot envia geradores para a Costa do Golfo *antes* de um furacão chegar à costa.
Qual princípio é esse?
- (A) Cross-docking
- (B) Amplificação do efeito chicote
- (C) Posicionamento de estoque sob restrições de lead time
- (D) Produção just-in-time
## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **Custo total posto** — o custo total entregue de um produto: preço de compra mais frete, tributos, custo de manutenção, liquidações e perdas por falta de estoque.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring** — transferir a produção para mais perto do mercado final, trocando um custo unitário maior por lead times menores e mais responsivos.

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **Markdown** — uma redução de preço aplicada para escoar estoque que não vendeu; um custo direto e mensurável de uma previsão ruim.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **Efeito chicote** — a amplificação das oscilações da demanda à medida que os pedidos sobem da ponta do varejo até o fornecedor.

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **Postponement** — manter um produto em forma genérica e sem comprometimento pelo maior tempo possível, para que a configuração final seja decidida quando a demanda for conhecida.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *Respostas: **1 — (B).** Lead times longos obrigam você a se comprometer com quantidades antes de saber o que vende; as unidades não vendidas são descontadas, e as liquidações normalmente superam em muito uma economia de compra de US$ 2 por unidade.

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — F.** Os estoques de segurança ajudaram a Toyota a continuar produzindo no início de 2021, enquanto concorrentes paralisavam linhas, mas, ainda naquele ano, fechamentos por causa da COVID em fornecedores do Sudeste Asiático forçaram cortes de produção mesmo assim.
A resiliência compra tempo, não imunidade.

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C).** Quando as estradas fecham, o tempo de reposição efetivamente se torna infinito, então o estoque precisa estar no lugar certo antes do evento. É uma decisão de posicionamento, não de produção ou de cross-docking.*

in.title: [Logistics 101 #15] Satu Jaket, Empat Belas Pelajaran: Menyatukan Seluruh Kursus

segments.src: > A supply chain is one long argument between speed, cost, and risk — and every company you shop at has picked a side.
segments.tr: > Rantai pasokan adalah satu argumen panjang antara kecepatan, biaya, dan risiko — dan setiap perusahaan tempat Anda berbelanja telah memilih salah satu sisi.
## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.
segments.tr: Ini adalah pemberhentian terakhir dalam kursus, jadi alih-alih alat baru, kita akan melakukan apa yang seharusnya dilakukan kelas terakhir: membedah satu perusahaan nyata, lalu menyebutkan beberapa gagasan yang terus muncul apa pun yang sedang Anda pindahkan.
**Studi kasus: Zara.**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: Zara dimiliki oleh Inditex, yang berkantor pusat di Arteixo, di barat laut Spanyol.

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: Para pesaingnya umumnya melakukan hal yang sudah jelas — merancang koleksi satu musim setahun sebelumnya, memesan dalam jumlah besar ke pabrik berbiaya terendah di Asia, lalu mengirimkannya melintasi Pasifik.

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: Cara itu menghasilkan biaya terendah *per unit*, yaitu angka yang paling mudah dipertahankan dalam rapat.
Zara membuat pilihan yang berbeda.

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: Barang yang sensitif terhadap tren — yang permintaannya tidak bisa diperkirakan — dibuat di Spanyol, Portugal, Maroko, dan Turki atau di dekat sana.

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: Barang dasar yang laku stabil sepanjang tahun, seperti kaus polos, tetap berasal dari pabrik berbiaya lebih rendah yang lebih jauh.

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: Toko menerima pengiriman sekitar dua kali seminggu, dalam jumlah kecil per model, dan manajer toko terus mengirimkan data penjualan serta reaksi pelanggan kembali ke pusat.

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: Jika suatu model tidak laku, hanya beberapa ratus unit yang ikut terbuang.

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: Jika laku, lebih banyak unit bisa sampai di toko dalam hitungan minggu, bukan musim.

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: Nearshoring membuat Zara mengeluarkan biaya lebih besar per pakaian.

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: Namun mereka mendapatkan kembali uang itu di tempat lain: menurut laporan luas, Zara memberi diskon pada porsi persediaan yang lebih kecil dibandingkan peritel fesyen pada umumnya, dan menjual lebih banyak produk dengan harga penuh.

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: Markdown adalah biaya nyata — hanya saja biaya itu tidak tercantum di anggaran manajer pengadaan.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: Itulah seluruh pelajaran kursus ini dalam satu perusahaan: **biaya satuan termurah bukanlah rantai pasokan termurah.** Dalam teks biasa:
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: Mengoptimalkan baris pertama sambil mengabaikan baris dua sampai lima adalah kesalahan mahal yang paling sering terjadi di bidang ini.

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **Lima gagasan yang terus dibahas dalam kursus:**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **Permintaan tidak pasti, dan ketidakpastian menimbulkan biaya.** Anda membayarnya baik sebagai persediaan yang tidak Anda butuhkan atau penjualan yang tidak bisa Anda capai. Anda memilih yang mana — Anda tidak bisa memilih untuk tidak membayar keduanya.

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **Informasi lebih berharga daripada persediaan.** Efek cambuk (bullwhip) — goyangan permintaan kecil yang membesar menjadi ayunan liar di hulu — pada dasarnya adalah kegagalan komunikasi, bukan masalah matematika.

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **Kecepatan menggantikan peramalan.** Jika waktu tunggu Anda dua minggu, Anda hampir tidak perlu memprediksi apa pun. Jika sembilan bulan, ramalan Anda yang menanggung seluruh beban.

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **Di mana Anda menyimpan persediaan sama pentingnya dengan berapa banyak.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — semuanya didasari naluri yang sama: tetap generik dan terpusat selama mungkin, berkomitmen selambat mungkin.

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **Efisiensi dan ketahanan saling tarik-menarik.** Setelah gempa Tōhoku 2011, Toyota memetakan lapisan pemasok terdalamnya dan meminta pemasok utama menyimpan stok penyangga semikonduktor — perilaku yang benar-benar tidak ramping. Ketika kelangkaan chip melanda awal 2021, penyangga itu memungkinkan Toyota terus memproduksi sementara pesaing menghentikan pabriknya. Ini bukan sihir: kemudian di 2021, penutupan akibat COVID di pemasok Asia Tenggara memaksa Toyota juga memangkas produksi. Ketahanan membeli waktu, bukan kekebalan.
## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: Perhatikan sebuah Home Depot di Pantai Teluk pada akhir Agustus.

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: Home Depot menjalankan pusat komando badai dari kantor pusatnya di Atlanta.

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: Beberapa hari sebelum badai mendarat, perusahaan mulai memindahkan generator, kayu lapis, air, terpal, dan baterai ke titik-titik persiapan dekat jalur prakiraan — sebelum satu pelanggan pun membeli barang, dan sebelum ada yang tahu kota mana yang persisnya akan terkena.

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: Setiap gagasan dari kursus ini ada dalam keputusan itu.

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **Peramalan:** kerucut badai adalah probabilitas, bukan janji.

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **Penempatan persediaan:** stok yang berada di Atlanta tidak berguna bagi pelanggan di Mobile pada hari Kamis; stok yang dikirim ke wilayah metro yang salah berarti sebuah truk penuh generator yang harus Anda angkut kembali.

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **Waktu tunggu:** begitu jalan raya ditutup, waktu pengisian ulang Anda berubah dari satu hari menjadi tak terhingga, sehingga keputusan harus diambil lebih awal dan kadang keliru.

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **Biaya total:** generator seharga $900 yang tiba seminggu terlambat memiliki nilai bagi pelanggan yang hampir nol, dan biaya reputasi dari rak kosong saat badai tidak tercantum di faktur mana pun.

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: Perusahaan yang melakukan pra-penempatan secara sadar menerima tambahan biaya pengiriman dan penanganan untuk menghindari biaya yang jauh lebih besar yang tidak bisa diukur dengan tepat.
Itu bukan trik logistik.
Itulah seluruh disiplin ilmunya.
## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. Zara membayar lebih mahal per pakaian untuk membuat barang tren di dekat rumah, dan mendapatkannya kembali dengan menjual lebih banyak pada harga penuh — bukti bahwa biaya satuan hanyalah satu baris dalam tagihan yang sebenarnya.

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. Tema-tema yang berulang: ketidakpastian selalu menimbulkan biaya, informasi menggantikan persediaan, kecepatan menggantikan peramalan, posisi lebih penting daripada jumlah, dan ketahanan dibeli, bukan gratis.

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. Setiap keputusan rantai pasokan adalah keputusan yang sama dengan pakaian yang berbeda — seberapa besar yang bersedia Anda bayar sekarang agar lebih sedikit salah di kemudian hari?
## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** Seorang manajer pengadaan beralih ke pabrik yang memangkas biaya satuan $2 per jaket, tetapi waktu tunggu naik dari 3 minggu menjadi 4 bulan.

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: Biaya mana yang PALING mungkin menghapus penghematan itu?
- (A) Biaya jasa kepabeanan

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) Markdown akhir musim untuk model yang tidak laku

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) Biaya perangkat lunak pesanan pembelian
- (D) Tenaga kerja toko

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** B/S — Penyangga chip pemasok Toyota, yang dibangun setelah gempa 2011, membuat perusahaan kebal terhadap kelangkaan semikonduktor 2021.

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** Home Depot mengirim generator ke arah Pantai Teluk *sebelum* badai mendarat.
Prinsip apa ini?
- (A) Cross-docking
- (B) Amplifikasi efek cambuk (bullwhip)
- (C) Penempatan persediaan di bawah kendala waktu tunggu
- (D) Produksi just-in-time
## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **Total landed cost** — biaya penuh produk yang sampai di tujuan: harga beli ditambah ongkos kirim, bea masuk, biaya penyimpanan, markdown, dan kerugian akibat kehabisan stok.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring** — memindahkan produksi lebih dekat ke pasar akhir, dengan menukar biaya satuan yang lebih tinggi dengan waktu tunggu yang lebih pendek dan lebih responsif.

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **Markdown** — pengurangan harga yang diambil untuk menghabiskan persediaan yang tidak laku; biaya langsung dan terukur dari peramalan yang buruk.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **Efek cambuk (bullwhip)** — amplifikasi ayunan permintaan saat pesanan bergerak ke hulu dari peritel ke pemasok.

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **Postponement** — menjaga produk dalam bentuk generik yang belum berkomitmen selama mungkin, agar konfigurasi akhirnya bisa diputuskan setelah permintaan diketahui.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **1 — (B).** Waktu tunggu yang panjang memaksa Anda berkomitmen pada jumlah sebelum tahu apa yang laku; unit yang tidak terjual akan didiskon, dan markdown biasanya jauh melebihi penghematan pengadaan $2 per unit.

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — S.** Penyangga itu membantu Toyota terus berproduksi pada awal 2021 ketika pesaing menghentikan lini mereka, tetapi di akhir tahun itu penutupan akibat COVID di pemasok Asia Tenggara tetap memaksa pemangkasan produksi.
Ketahanan membeli waktu, bukan kekebalan.

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C).** Begitu jalan ditutup, waktu tunggu pengisian ulang secara efektif menjadi tak terhingga, sehingga persediaan harus sudah berada di tempat yang tepat sebelum peristiwa terjadi — keputusan penempatan, bukan keputusan produksi atau cross-docking.*

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.

**ケーススタディ：ZARA。**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: ZARAはInditexグループの一員で、本社はスペイン北西部のアルテイショにあります。

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: 競合の多くはわかりやすいやり方をとります。シーズンの1年前にデザインを決め、アジアの最低コストの工場に大量発注し、太平洋を越えて輸送します。

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: これにより単位当たりのコストは最も低くなり、会議で最も説明しやすい数字になります。
ZARAは別のトレードオフを選びました。

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: トレンドに敏感な商品、つまり誰も需要を予測できない商品は、スペイン、ポルトガル、モロッコ、トルコの国内または近隣で生産されます。

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: 一年中安定して売れる定番商品、たとえば無地のTシャツなどは、今も遠くの低コストの工場で生産されています。

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: 店舗には週におよそ2回、スタイルごとに少量ずつ商品が届き、店長は販売実績と顧客の反応を絶えず本部にフィードバックします。

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: ある商品が売れなくても、失われるのは数百点だけです。

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: 売れ行きが良ければ、シーズンを待たずに数週間で追加の商品を店頭に並べられます。

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: ニアショアリングは、1着あたりのコストをZARAにとって高くします。

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: しかし、その分は別の場所で取り戻しています。一般に報告されているところでは、一般的なファストファッション小売業者よりも在庫の値下げ率が低く、定価でより多くの商品を売っています。

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: 値下げは実際のコストです。ただ、それは仕入担当者の予算項目には表れないだけです。

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: これがこのコース全体の教訓を一社で示したものです。**最も安い単位コストが、最も安いサプライチェーンとは限らない。** 平たく言えば：
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: 1行目だけを最適化して、2行目から5行目を無視することは、この分野で最もよくある高くつく失敗です。

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **コースで繰り返し取り上げた5つのアイデア：**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **需要は不確実であり、不確実性にはコストがかかる。** そのコストは、必要のなかった在庫か、売れなかった販売機会のどちらかとして支払うことになります。どちらを選ぶかは決められますが、どちらも選ばないことはできません。

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **情報は在庫に勝る。** ブルウィップ効果、つまり需要の小さな揺れが上流で大きな変動に増幅される現象は、計算の問題というより、主に情報伝達の失敗です。

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **スピードは需要予測の代わりになる。** リードタイムが2週間なら、ほとんど予測の必要はありません。9か月なら、予測がすべての仕事を担うことになります。

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **在庫をどこに置くかは、どれだけ置くかと同じくらい重要。** 延期、プーリング、クロスドッキングはすべて同じ発想です。できるだけ汎用的で中央に置いたまま、できるだけ遅くコミットする。

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **効率性とレジリエンスは反対方向に引っ張り合う。** 2011年の東日本大震災の後、トヨタは深い階層の取引先まで把握し、主要サプライヤーに半導体の緩衝在庫を持たせました。これは本当に「リーン」ではない行動です。2021年初めに半導体不足が起きたとき、この緩衝在庫によりトヨタは生産を続けられ、競合が工場を止めるなか生産を維持しました。ただし魔法ではありませんでした。2021年後半には、東南アジアのサプライヤーでのCOVIDによる操業停止で、トヨタも結局減産を余儀なくされました。レジリエンスが買えるのは時間であって、免疫ではありません。
## 日常生活で

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: 8月下旬のメキシコ湾岸にあるHome Depotを見てみましょう。

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: Home Depotはアトランタの本社で、ハリケーン対策の指令センターを運営しています。

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: 上陸の数日前から、同社は発電機、合板、水、防水シート、電池を、予想進路付近の集積拠点へ移し始めます。顧客が一点も買う前に、そしてどの都市が直撃されるかが正確にわかる前に、です。

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: このコースのアイデアはすべて、この判断の中にあります。

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **需要予測：** 台風の予報円は確率であって、約束ではありません。

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **在庫配置：** アトランタにある在庫は、木曜日にモービルにいる顧客の役には立ちません。一方、間違った都市圏に送った在庫は、持ち帰らなければならない発電機のトラック一台分になります。

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **リードタイム：** 高速道路が封鎖されると、補充にかかる時間は1日から無限大になるため、判断は早めに下す必要があり、ときには外れることも受け入れなければなりません。

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **総コスト：** 1週間遅れて届いた900ドルの発電機の顧客にとっての価値はほぼゼロです。嵐の最中に棚が空になることによる評判の損失は、どの請求書にも載りません。

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: 事前に配置する企業は、正確に測ることのできない、はるかに大きなコストを避けるために、余分な輸送費と取扱費を意図的に受け入れているのです。
これは物流のちょっとした小技ではありません。
これこそ、この分野の全体なのです。
## 3行まとめ

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. ZARAは、トレンド商品を国内に近い場所で作るために1着あたりの費用を多く払い、定価でより多く売ることでそれを取り戻しています。単位コストは、実際の総費用の一項目にすぎないことの証明です。

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. 繰り返し現れるテーマ：不確実性は必ずコストを伴う、情報は在庫の代わりになる、スピードは予測の代わりになる、位置は数量に勝る、そしてレジリエンスは自然に得られるものではなく、お金で買うものである。

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. どのサプライチェーンの判断も、服装を変えただけで同じ一つの判断です。将来より正しくあるために、今どれだけ支払う覚悟があるか。
## ✅ 自己確認クイズ

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** 仕入担当者が、ジャケット1着あたりの単価を2ドル下げる工場に切り替えました。しかしリードタイムは3週間から4か月に延びます。

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: その節約分を最も帳消しにしそうなコストはどれでしょう？
- (A) 通関業者の手数料

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) 売れなかったスタイルのシーズン末の値下げ

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) 発注書ソフトウェアの費用
- (D) 店舗の人件費

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** ○/× — 2011年の地震の後に作ったトヨタの取引先の半導体緩衝在庫により、同社は2021年の半導体不足の影響を受けなくなった。

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** Home Depotは、ハリケーンが上陸する*前に*、発電機をメキシコ湾岸に向けて出荷します。
これはどの原則でしょう？
- (A) クロスドッキング
- (B) ブルウィップ効果による増幅
- (C) リードタイム制約下での在庫配置
- (D) ジャスト・イン・タイム生産
## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **総陸揚げコスト（Total landed cost）** — 製品が届くまでにかかる総コスト。仕入価格に、輸送費、関税、在庫保管費、値下げ、品切れによる損失を加えたもの。

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **ニアショアリング（Nearshoring）** — 生産を最終市場の近くに移すこと。単位コストは上がるが、リードタイムが短くなり、対応が速くなる。

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **値下げ（Markdown）** — 売れなかった在庫を処分するために行う値下げ。悪い需要予測による、直接測定できるコスト。

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **ブルウィップ効果（Bullwhip effect）** — 注文が小売から供給元へ上流に伝わるにつれて、需要の変動が増幅されること。

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **延期（Postponement）** — 最終的な構成を需要が分かるまで決めずに、製品を汎用的で確定していない状態のまま保つこと。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *正解：**1 — (B)。** 長いリードタイムのため、何が売れるかを知る前に数量を確定しなければなりません。売れなかった在庫は値下げされ、その値下げ額は、1個あたり2ドルの仕入れの節約よりも通常はるかに大きくなります。

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — ×。** 緩衝在庫により、2021年初めには競合が生産ラインを止めるなか、トヨタは生産を続けられました。しかし同年後半には、東南アジアのサプライヤーでのCOVIDによる操業停止により、結局生産を削減せざるを得ませんでした。
レジリエンスが買えるのは時間であって、免疫ではありません。

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C)。** 道路が封鎖されると、補充のリードタイムは実質的に無限大になるため、在庫はイベントの前に正しい場所になければなりません。これは生産や中継の判断ではなく、配置の判断です。*

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **Fünf Ideen, zu denen der Kurs immer wieder zurückkehrte:**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **Die Nachfrage ist unsicher, und Unsicherheit kostet Geld.** Sie zahlen dafür entweder mit Lagerbeständen, die Sie nicht gebraucht hätten, oder mit Verkäufen, die Sie nicht tätigen konnten. Sie können wählen, welches – aber nicht, keines von beiden zu zahlen.

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **Wo Sie Bestand halten, ist genauso wichtig wie wie viel.** Postponement, Pooling, Cross-Docking – alles dasselbe Prinzip: so lange wie möglich generisch und zentral bleiben, so spät wie möglich festlegen.

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **Effizienz und Resilienz ziehen in entgegengesetzte Richtungen.** Nach dem Erdbeben von Tōhoku 2011 kartierte Toyota seine tiefen Zuliefererebenen und ließ wichtige Zulieferer Pufferbestände an Halbleitern halten – ein wirklich unschlankes Verhalten. Als im Frühjahr 2021 der Chipmangel einsetzte, ermöglichte dieser Puffer Toyota, weiter zu produzieren, während Wettbewerber Werke stilllegen mussten. Es war keine Magie: Später im Jahr 2021 zwangen COVID-bedingte Schließungen bei Zulieferern in Südostasien Toyota dennoch, die Produktion zu drosseln. Resilienz kauft Zeit, keine Immunität.

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **Lieferzeit:** Sobald die Autobahnen gesperrt sind, wird Ihre Wiederbeschaffungszeit von einem Tag auf unendlich, also muss die Entscheidung früh fallen und manchmal falsch sein.

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **Gesamtkosten:** Ein 900-Dollar-Generator, der eine Woche zu spät eintrifft, hat einen Kundennutzen von praktisch null, und der Imageschaden durch leere Regale während eines Sturms lässt sich auf keiner Rechnung beziffern.

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: Das Unternehmen, das vorab positioniert, nimmt bewusst zusätzliche Fracht- und Abwicklungskosten in Kauf, um einen viel größeren Kostenblock zu vermeiden, den es nicht genau messen kann.
Das ist kein Logistik-Trick.
Das ist die gesamte Disziplin.
## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Zara pays more per garment to make trend items close to home, and earns it back by selling more at full price — proof that unit cost is only one line in the real bill.
segments.tr: 1. Zara zahlt pro Kleidungsstück mehr, um Trendartikel nah am Markt herzustellen, und verdient dies zurück, indem es mehr zum vollen Preis verkauft – der Beweis, dass der Stückpreis nur eine Zeile der tatsächlichen Rechnung ist.

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. Die wiederkehrenden Themen: Unsicherheit kostet immer etwas, Information ersetzt Lagerbestand, Geschwindigkeit ersetzt Prognosen, Position schlägt Menge, und Resilienz wird gekauft, nicht geschenkt.

segments.src: 3. Every supply chain decision is the same decision in different clothes — how much are you willing to pay now to be less wrong later?
segments.tr: 3. Jede Entscheidung in der Lieferkette ist dieselbe Entscheidung in anderem Gewand – wie viel sind Sie bereit, jetzt zu zahlen, um später weniger falsch zu liegen?
## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.src: **1.** A sourcing manager switches to a factory that cuts unit cost by $2 per jacket, but lead time goes from 3 weeks to 4 months.
segments.tr: **1.** Ein Einkaufsleiter wechselt zu einer Fabrik, die den Stückpreis um 2 Dollar pro Jacke senkt, aber die Lieferzeit von 3 Wochen auf 4 Monate erhöht.

segments.src: Which cost is MOST likely to erase the savings?
segments.tr: Welche Kosten machen die Einsparung MOST wahrscheinlich zunichte?
- (A) Zollabfertigungsgebühren

segments.src: - (B) End-of-season markdowns on styles that didn't sell
segments.tr: - (B) Saisonschlussreduzierungen bei Modellen, die sich nicht verkauft haben

segments.src: - (C) The cost of the purchase order software
segments.tr: - (C) Die Kosten der Software für Bestellungen
- (D) Personalkosten in den Filialen

segments.src: **2.** O/X — Toyota's supplier chip buffers, built after the 2011 earthquake, made the company immune to the 2021 semiconductor shortage.
segments.tr: **2.** Richtig/Falsch – Die nach dem Erdbeben 2011 aufgebauten Chip-Puffer bei Zulieferern machten das Unternehmen gegen den Halbleitermangel 2021 immun.

segments.src: **3.** Home Depot ships generators toward the Gulf Coast *before* a hurricane makes landfall.
segments.tr: **3.** Home Depot verschickt Generatoren an die Golfküste, *bevor* ein Hurrikan auf Land trifft.
Welches Prinzip steckt dahinter?
- (A) Cross-Docking
- (B) Bullwhip-Verstärkung
- (C) Bestandspositionierung unter Lieferzeitbeschränkungen
- (D) Just-in-Time-Produktion
## 📚 Begriffe des Tages

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **Total Landed Cost** – die vollständigen Lieferkosten eines Produkts: Kaufpreis plus Fracht, Zölle, Lagerkosten, Preisreduzierungen und Verluste durch Fehlbestände.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring** – die Verlagerung der Produktion näher an den Endmarkt, wobei höhere Stückkosten gegen kürzere, reaktionsschnellere Lieferzeiten getauscht werden.

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **Preisreduzierung (Markdown)** – eine Preissenkung, um nicht verkaufte Bestände abzubauen; ein direkter, messbarer Kostenfaktor einer falschen Prognose.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **Bullwhip-Effekt** – die Verstärkung von Nachfrageschwankungen, wenn Bestellungen vom Händler zum Lieferanten flussaufwärts wandern.

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **Postponement** – ein Produkt so lange wie möglich in generischer, noch nicht festgelegter Form zu halten, damit die endgültige Konfiguration erst entschieden wird, wenn die Nachfrage bekannt ist.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *Lösungen: **1 — (B).** Lange Lieferzeiten zwingen dazu, Mengen festzulegen, bevor man weiß, was sich verkauft; die unverkauften Stücke werden reduziert, und die Preisnachlässe übersteigen typischerweise eine Einsparung von 2 Dollar pro Stück bei Weitem.

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — X.** Die Puffer halfen Toyota, Anfang 2021 weiter zu produzieren, während Wettbewerber Linien stilllegten, aber später in diesem Jahr zwangen COVID-Schließungen bei Zulieferern in Südostasien trotzdem zu Produktionskürzungen.
Resilienz kauft Zeit, keine Immunität.

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C).** Sobald die Straßen gesperrt sind, wird die Wiederbeschaffungszeit faktisch unendlich, daher muss der Bestand vor dem Ereignis am richtigen Ort sein – eine Positionierungsentscheidung, keine Produktions- oder Docking-Entscheidung.*

vi.title: [Logistics 101 #15] Một chiếc áo khoác, mười bốn bài học: Tổng hợp cả khóa học

segments.src: > A supply chain is one long argument between speed, cost, and risk — and every company you shop at has picked a side.
segments.tr: > Chuỗi cung ứng là một cuộc tranh luận dài giữa tốc độ, chi phí và rủi ro — và mỗi công ty bạn mua sắm đều đã chọn một phía.
## Nội dung hôm nay

segments.src: This is the last stop in the course, so instead of a new tool we'll do what a final class should do: take one real company apart, then name the handful of ideas that keep showing up no matter what you're moving.
segments.tr: Đây là điểm dừng cuối cùng của khóa học, nên thay vì giới thiệu một công cụ mới, chúng ta sẽ làm điều mà một buổi học cuối cùng nên làm: phân tích một công ty thực tế, rồi nêu tên một số ý tưởng cốt lõi luôn xuất hiện bất kể bạn đang vận chuyển thứ gì.
**Trường hợp nghiên cứu: Zara.**

segments.src: Zara belongs to Inditex, headquartered in Arteixo, in northwestern Spain.
segments.tr: Zara thuộc về Inditex, có trụ sở tại Arteixo, phía tây bắc Tây Ban Nha.

segments.src: Its competitors mostly do the obvious thing — design a season a year ahead, place enormous orders with the lowest-cost factories in Asia, and ship them across the Pacific.
segments.tr: Các đối thủ của hãng phần lớn làm điều hiển nhiên — thiết kế một mùa trước cả năm, đặt những đơn hàng khổng lồ tại các nhà máy chi phí thấp nhất ở châu Á, rồi vận chuyển qua Thái Bình Dương.

segments.src: That produces the lowest cost *per unit*, which is the number most easily defended in a meeting.
segments.tr: Cách này tạo ra chi phí thấp nhất *trên mỗi sản phẩm*, là con số dễ bảo vệ nhất trong một cuộc họp.
Zara chọn một sự đánh đổi khác.

segments.src: Trend-sensitive items — the ones nobody can forecast — are made in or near Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Turkey.
segments.tr: Những mặt hàng nhạy cảm với xu hướng — loại mà không ai dự báo được — được sản xuất tại Tây Ban Nha, Bồ Đào Nha, Morocco và Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ hoặc ở gần đó.

segments.src: Basics that sell steadily all year, like plain T-shirts, still come from lower-cost factories farther away.
segments.tr: Các mặt hàng cơ bản bán đều quanh năm, như áo phông trơn, vẫn đến từ các nhà máy chi phí thấp hơn nhưng ở xa hơn.

segments.src: Stores get shipments roughly twice a week, in small quantities per style, and store managers feed sales and customer reactions back constantly.
segments.tr: Các cửa hàng nhận hàng khoảng hai lần mỗi tuần, số lượng nhỏ cho mỗi mẫu, và quản lý cửa hàng liên tục gửi phản hồi về doanh số và phản ứng của khách hàng.

segments.src: If a style dies, only a few hundred units die with it.
segments.tr: Nếu một mẫu không bán được, chỉ vài trăm sản phẩm bị thiệt hại.

segments.src: If it sells, more can be in stores in weeks rather than seasons.
segments.tr: Nếu mẫu bán chạy, có thể đưa thêm hàng ra cửa hàng trong vài tuần thay vì vài mùa.

segments.src: Nearshoring costs Zara more per garment.
segments.tr: Nearshoring khiến Zara tốn nhiều chi phí hơn cho mỗi sản phẩm.

segments.src: It wins the money back somewhere else: it is widely reported to discount a smaller share of its inventory than typical fashion retailers, and it sells more product at full price.
segments.tr: Nhưng hãng bù lại ở chỗ khác: theo báo cáo rộng rãi, Zara giảm giá một tỷ lệ hàng tồn kho nhỏ hơn so với các nhà bán lẻ thời trang thông thường, và bán được nhiều sản phẩm hơn với giá gốc.

segments.src: A markdown is a real cost — it just doesn't sit in the sourcing manager's budget line.
segments.tr: Giảm giá xả hàng là một chi phí thực sự — chỉ là nó không nằm trong dòng ngân sách của bộ phận mua hàng.

segments.src: That's the whole lesson of the course in one company: **the cheapest unit cost is not the cheapest supply chain.** In plain text:
segments.tr: Đó là toàn bộ bài học của khóa học gói gọn trong một công ty: **chi phí đơn vị thấp nhất không phải là chuỗi cung ứng rẻ nhất.** Viết thành văn bản thuần:
Total landed cost = unit cost
+ freight + duties
+ inventory carrying cost
+ markdowns
+ lost sales from stockouts

segments.src: Optimizing line one while ignoring lines two through five is the single most common expensive mistake in this field.
segments.tr: Tối ưu dòng một mà bỏ qua dòng hai đến dòng năm là sai lầm tốn kém nhất và phổ biến nhất trong lĩnh vực này.

segments.src: **Five ideas the course kept returning to:**
segments.tr: **Năm ý tưởng mà khóa học liên tục quay lại:**

segments.src: 1. **Demand is uncertain, and uncertainty costs money.** You pay for it either as inventory you didn't need or sales you couldn't make. You choose which — you don't get to choose neither.
segments.tr: 1. **Nhu cầu không chắc chắn, và sự không chắc chắn tốn tiền.** Bạn trả giá cho nó dưới dạng hàng tồn kho không cần thiết hoặc doanh số không thể đạt được. Bạn chọn cái nào — bạn không được chọn cả hai đều không.

segments.src: 2. **Information beats inventory.** The bullwhip effect — small demand wobbles amplifying into wild swings upstream — is mostly a communication failure, not a math problem.
segments.tr: 2. **Thông tin quan trọng hơn hàng tồn kho.** Hiệu ứng roi da — những dao động nhỏ của nhu cầu bị khuếch đại thành biến động lớn ở phía thượng nguồn — chủ yếu là lỗi giao tiếp chứ không phải bài toán toán học.

segments.src: 3. **Speed is a substitute for forecasting.** If your lead time is two weeks, you barely need to predict anything. If it's nine months, your forecast is doing all the work.
segments.tr: 3. **Tốc độ là sự thay thế cho dự báo.** Nếu thời gian giao hàng của bạn là hai tuần, bạn hầu như không cần dự đoán gì. Nếu là chín tháng, dự báo của bạn phải làm toàn bộ việc.

segments.src: 4. **Where you hold inventory matters as much as how much.** Postponement, pooling, cross-docking — all the same instinct: stay generic and central as long as possible, commit as late as possible.
segments.tr: 4. **Vị trí đặt hàng tồn kho quan trọng ngang với số lượng.** Trì hoãn (postponement), gộp hàng (pooling), cross-docking — tất cả đều cùng một bản năng: giữ hàng ở dạng chung và tập trung càng lâu càng tốt, cam kết càng muộn càng tốt.

segments.src: 5. **Efficiency and resilience pull in opposite directions.** After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, Toyota mapped its deep supplier tiers and had key suppliers hold buffer stock of semiconductors — genuinely un-lean behavior. When the chip shortage hit in early 2021, that buffer let Toyota keep building while rivals idled plants. It wasn't magic: later in 2021, COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced Toyota to cut output too. Resilience buys you time, not immunity.
segments.tr: 5. **Hiệu quả và khả năng phục hồi đi ngược chiều nhau.** Sau trận động đất Tōhoku năm 2011, Toyota lập bản đồ các tầng nhà cung cấp sâu của mình và yêu cầu các nhà cung cấp chủ chốt giữ tồn kho đệm chất bán dẫn — một hành vi thực sự không tinh gọn. Khi tình trạng thiếu chip bùng phát đầu năm 2021, lượng đệm đó giúp Toyota tiếp tục sản xuất trong khi các đối thủ phải dừng nhà máy. Điều này không phải phép màu: cuối năm 2021, việc đóng cửa do COVID tại các nhà cung cấp ở Đông Nam Á cũng buộc Toyota cắt giảm sản lượng. Khả năng phục hồi mua cho bạn thời gian, không phải miễn nhiễm.
## Trong đời sống hằng ngày

segments.src: Watch a Home Depot on the Gulf Coast in late August.
segments.tr: Hãy quan sát một cửa hàng Home Depot ở vùng Vịnh Mexico vào cuối tháng Tám.

segments.src: Home Depot runs a hurricane command center out of its Atlanta headquarters.
segments.tr: Home Depot vận hành một trung tâm chỉ huy bão từ trụ sở tại Atlanta.

segments.src: Days before landfall, the company starts moving generators, plywood, water, tarps, and batteries toward staging points near the forecast track — before any customer has bought a single item, and before anyone knows exactly which city gets hit.
segments.tr: Vài ngày trước khi bão đổ bộ, công ty bắt đầu chuyển máy phát điện, ván ép, nước, bạt và pin đến các điểm tập kết gần đường đi dự báo — trước khi có bất kỳ khách hàng nào mua một món hàng nào, và trước khi ai biết chính xác thành phố nào sẽ bị ảnh hưởng.

segments.src: Every idea from this course is in that decision.
segments.tr: Mọi ý tưởng trong khóa học này đều có mặt trong quyết định đó.

segments.src: **Forecasting:** the storm cone is a probability, not a promise.
segments.tr: **Dự báo:** vùng ảnh hưởng của bão là một xác suất, không phải lời hứa.

segments.src: **Inventory positioning:** stock sitting in Atlanta is useless to a customer in Mobile on Thursday; stock pushed to the wrong metro is a truckload of generators you now have to haul back.
segments.tr: **Vị trí tồn kho:** hàng đặt ở Atlanta vô dụng với khách hàng ở Mobile vào thứ Năm; hàng bị đẩy nhầm đến thành phố sai là một xe tải máy phát điện mà bạn phải chở về.

segments.src: **Lead time:** once the highways close, your replenishment time goes from one day to infinity, so the decision has to be made early and be wrong sometimes.
segments.tr: **Thời gian giao hàng:** khi đường cao tốc đóng lại, thời gian bổ sung hàng của bạn chuyển từ một ngày thành vô hạn, nên quyết định phải được đưa ra sớm và đôi khi sẽ sai.

segments.src: **Total cost:** a $900 generator that arrives a week late has a customer-value of roughly zero, and the reputational cost of empty shelves during a storm doesn't fit on any invoice.
segments.tr: **Tổng chi phí:** một máy phát điện 900 đô la đến trễ một tuần có giá trị đối với khách hàng gần như bằng không, và chi phí uy tín khi kệ hàng trống trong bão không nằm trên bất kỳ hóa đơn nào.

segments.src: The company that pre-positions is knowingly accepting extra freight and handling cost to avoid a much larger cost it can't measure precisely.
segments.tr: Công ty chủ động đặt hàng trước đang cố ý chấp nhận chi phí vận chuyển và xử lý thêm để tránh một chi phí lớn hơn nhiều mà họ không thể đo lường chính xác.
Đó không phải là một mánh khóe logistics.
Đó chính là toàn bộ ngành nghề.
## Tóm tắt trong ba dòng

segments.src: 2. The recurring themes: uncertainty always costs something, information substitutes for inventory, speed substitutes for forecasting, position beats quantity, and resilience is bought, not free.
segments.tr: 2. Các chủ đề lặp lại: sự không chắc chắn luôn tốn kém, thông tin thay thế cho hàng tồn kho, tốc độ thay thế cho dự báo, vị trí quan trọng hơn số lượng, và khả năng phục hồi phải được mua chứ không miễn phí.

segments.tr: 3. Mọi quyết định trong chuỗi cung ứng đều là cùng một quyết định khoác bộ quần áo khác — bạn sẵn sàng trả bao nhiêu ngay bây giờ để ít sai hơn về sau?

## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Total landed cost** — the full delivered cost of a product: purchase price plus freight, duties, carrying cost, markdowns, and stockout losses.
segments.tr: - **Tổng chi phí giao hàng (Total landed cost)** — toàn bộ chi phí giao đến tay của một sản phẩm: giá mua cộng với cước vận chuyển, thuế nhập khẩu, chi phí lưu kho, giảm giá xả hàng và tổn thất do hết hàng.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring** — moving production closer to the end market, trading higher unit cost for shorter, more responsive lead times.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring** — đưa sản xuất đến gần thị trường tiêu thụ, đánh đổi chi phí đơn vị cao hơn lấy thời gian giao hàng ngắn hơn và phản ứng nhanh hơn.

segments.src: - **Markdown** — a price reduction taken to clear inventory that didn't sell; a direct, measurable cost of a bad forecast.
segments.tr: - **Giảm giá xả hàng (Markdown)** — việc giảm giá nhằm thanh lý hàng tồn không bán được; là chi phí trực tiếp, đo lường được của một dự báo sai.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — the amplification of demand swings as orders travel upstream from retailer to supplier.
segments.tr: - **Hiệu ứng roi da (Bullwhip effect)** — sự khuếch đại biến động nhu cầu khi các đơn hàng đi ngược lên từ nhà bán lẻ đến nhà cung cấp.

segments.src: - **Postponement** — keeping a product in a generic, uncommitted form as long as possible so the final configuration can be decided once demand is known.
segments.tr: - **Trì hoãn (Postponement)** — giữ sản phẩm ở dạng chung, chưa cam kết càng lâu càng tốt để có thể quyết định cấu hình cuối cùng khi nhu cầu đã rõ.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B).** Long lead times force you to commit to quantities before you know what sells; the unsold units get discounted, and the markdowns typically dwarf a $2-per-unit sourcing saving.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: **1 — (B).** Thời gian giao hàng dài buộc bạn phải cam kết số lượng trước khi biết hàng nào bán chạy; số hàng không bán được sẽ bị giảm giá, và các khoản giảm giá thường lớn hơn nhiều so với khoản tiết kiệm 2 đô la mỗi sản phẩm từ việc mua hàng.

segments.src: **2 — X.** The buffers helped Toyota keep producing early in 2021 while competitors idled lines, but later that year COVID shutdowns at Southeast Asian suppliers forced production cuts anyway.
segments.tr: **2 — X.** Tồn kho đệm giúp Toyota duy trì sản xuất vào đầu năm 2021 trong khi các đối thủ phải dừng dây chuyền, nhưng cuối năm đó việc đóng cửa do COVID tại các nhà cung cấp ở Đông Nam Á vẫn buộc phải cắt giảm sản xuất.
Khả năng phục hồi mua thời gian, không mua được sự miễn nhiễm.

segments.src: **3 — (C).** Once the roads close, replenishment lead time effectively becomes infinite, so the inventory has to be in the right place before the event — a positioning decision, not a production or docking one.*
segments.tr: **3 — (C).** Khi đường đã đóng, thời gian bổ sung hàng thực tế trở nên vô hạn, nên hàng tồn kho phải có mặt đúng chỗ trước khi sự kiện xảy ra — đây là quyết định về vị trí, không phải về sản xuất hay cross-docking.*
